name: Command Deck
narrativeOnEnter: The nerve centre of Meridian Station. Wide viewport looking out at open space — the rescue shuttle is clearly visible, holding position. Navigation terminals, captain's station, comms systems. A locked command locker sits against the far wall.

action.text:
CAPTAIN'S LOG — FINAL ENTRY

'Reactor alarm at 03:10. Ordered full crew evacuation — Kovalev stayed to attempt manual stabilisation. I should have ordered everyone off.

Distress beacon is active via the comms array — rescue shuttle is holding at 800m.
Escape pod launch code is 5519 — Kovalev and Chen both know it.

If anyone finds this log: stabilise the reactor first.
Then get to the pod bay. Then go home.

— Captain Diaz, Meridian Station Alpha'

The rescue shuttle is visible through the viewport — holding at exactly 800 metres. Standard evacuation protocol: hold position, wait for beacon signal, approach on confirmation.

They're out there. Waiting. They've been waiting since 03:14.

Through the external hull, you can just make out an access port. It's an external airlock — rarely used, but it connects directly to the docking ring. If the station's internal systems are compromised, that might be your backup route.

Navigation console for Meridian Station Alpha. Orbital positioning, thruster control, docking systems.

All systems showing nominal — the station's position is stable.

One readout is blinking: 'RESCUE SHUTTLE MERIDIAN-3 — HOLDING. AWAITING BEACON CONFIRMATION.'

The distress beacon is in the Comms Array.

hotspots.label: Lock Station & Signal All Clear
hotspots.lockedMessage: Reactor must be stabilised before you can lock the station down.
